jobs.title: Staff Software Engineer, AI Developer Tooling
jobs.description:
About Sentry

Software runs the world and the pace is faster than ever. Sentry helps developers fix errors and performance issues before users notice, so teams can spend less time firefighting and more time building.

Trusted by 200,000+ organizations, Sentry is today’s application monitoring standard and our team is building its AI-native future.

About The Role

You’ll own AI-assisted coding within Sentry’s Platform Engineering organization, building the systems and workflows AI coding agents need to contribute reliably to our codebase. Your work will span engineering teams, with Developer Infrastructure as your home base.

Your first focus will be making internal developer systems accessible to agents. Many workflows currently depend on human interaction through a UI. You’ll identify the most valuable gaps, expose those capabilities through APIs, and connect tools such as Claude Code to complete development workflows.

From there, you’ll improve the quality of AI-generated pull requests and automate recurring engineering work, including dependency upgrades, minor bug fixes, and maintenance. You’ll build the context and execution environment agents need: relevant repository information, tools and permissions, state management, tests, logs, recovery mechanisms, and evaluations.

You’ll partner with engineers across Sentry to understand where agents succeed, where they fail, and which changes improve the development process. This role combines technical direction with hands-on implementation, from choosing the problems to solve through building, measuring, and improving the solutions.

This role is based in San Francisco, with three days per week in the office to work closely with Platform teams and engineering leadership.

What You’ll Do

Set priorities for AI-assisted development at Sentry, using engineer feedback and workflow data to identify where agents would provide the most value.
Make internal developer systems accessible through APIs and build integrations enabling agents to complete workflows across those systems.
Build context systems and agent execution tooling, including tool access, permissions, checkpoints, retries, and logging.
Develop automated checks, evaluations, and feedback loops to improve the correctness, maintainability, and review readiness of AI-generated pull requests.
Automate recurring work such as security dependency upgrades, minor bug fixes, and routine maintenance.
Improve supporting developer workflows, including issue triage and CI/CD, where they limit agent effectiveness or create repetitive work for engineers.
Lead changes across engineering teams, build agreement on priorities, and measure whether the tools reduce manual work and improve delivery.

How You Work

You’ve used AI coding agents on real development work and have informed views on their strengths, limitations, and failure modes.
You bring structure to ambiguous problems, choose a practical starting point, and follow through on delivery.
You move comfortably between infrastructure, backend systems, and developer tooling.
You know when to build, integrate an existing tool, involve another team, or stop work with limited value.
You combine data with direct feedback from engineers to assess whether a solution improves their work.
You explain technical tradeoffs clearly and build alignment across teams and senior leadership.

Qualifications

10+ years of software engineering experience, including hands-on ownership of production systems.
Experience building developer tools, infrastructure, or automation used by engineering teams, such as CI/CD systems, internal APIs, code review tooling, or agent workflows.
Hands-on experience using AI coding tools and agents, with an understanding of how context, tool access, and validation affect their output. Prior machine learning experience is not required.
Strong software engineering and system design fundamentals, including experience building reliable integrations across systems.
A track record of leading cross-team technical initiatives from problem definition through implementation and adoption.
Clear written and verbal communication, including explaining technical decisions and recommendations to senior engineering leaders.

Nice to Have

Experience building agent harnesses, context systems, evaluations, or automated pull request workflows.
Experience with code review tooling, static analysis, or automated testing.
Experience measuring and improving developer experience or engineering productivity.
Experience with large-scale distributed systems or monolith decomposition.
Public contributions to developer tooling or AI-assisted development projects.

The base salary range that Sentry reasonably expects to pay for this position is $220,000 to $400,000 USD, plus an annual performance bonus of up to 15% of base salary. A successful candidate’s actual base salary (or hourly wage) amount will be determined by a variety of relevant factors including, without limitation, the candidate’s work location, education, work and other relevant experience, skills, and job-related knowledge. A successful candidate will be eligible to participate in Sentry’s employee benefit plans/programs applicable to the candidate’s position (including incentive compensation, equity grants, paid time off, and group health insurance coverage). See Sentry Benefits for more details about the Company’s benefit plans/programs.

Equal Opportunity at Sentry

Sentry is committed to providing equal employment opportunities to its employees and candidates for employment regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, veteran status, or other legally-protected characteristic. This commitment includes the provision of reasonable accommodations to employees and candidates for employment with physical or mental disabilities who require such accommodations in order to (a) perform the essential functions of their jobs, or (b) seek employment with Sentry. We strive to build a diverse team, with an inclusive culture where every teammate can thrive. Sentry is an open-source company because we believe that everyone, everywhere, should have the ability and tools to make great software. Software should be accessible. That starts with making our industry accessible.

If you need assistance or an accommodation due to a disability, you may contact us at accommodations@sentry.io.

jobs.title: Member of the Technical Staff - Solution Architect and Evangelist
jobs.description:
Alice sells to the frontier labs. Those conversations open as a technical question. You sit in the room, understand the lab's real system, and design the engagement.
The role will leverage the West Coast presence and engagement.

Key Responsibilities:

1. Be the technical front line in the Bay Area

You are the Tier 1 technical voice in client meetings, RFPs and novel scopes. Take the deep discovery conversation, then convert it into a scope that research and delivery can execute.
You own the top and middle of the funnel. Create the conversation. Earn the technical win. Define the partnership. Sales owns the commercial close.
You will handle objections in live technical deep dives with elite engineering and research teams, without escalating every time.
2. Build the frontier-lab community in the Valley

Run small, high-signal events with post-training, safety and security leads from the labs. We run roughly ten Bay Area events a year, including closed sessions for our circle of experts.
Brand awareness is a by-product. The purpose is to learn what those teams need, in their language, and to set up the meetings that turn into clients.
Represent Alice where it matters: conferences, analyst briefings, technical talks, joint research.
3. Close the field-to-strategy loop

Carry market- signal back into the company and act on it. Work with the CTO to name the next needle mover before it shows up in an RFP, then push it into the roadmap.
You influence the AI Labs pod agenda, AI security research priorities, and product direction directly.
4. Be a pillar to build around

Set the terms for how Alice operates in the Valley. Be the key person on the ground. Interview for adjacent roles, help other departments hire here, and carry the Alice name locally.

Must Have:

8+ relevant years of experience as a Principal Solution Architect.
Deep, current understanding of AI systems security: agents, tools, orchestration, data flow, guardrails, red teaming, evals. Model-layer knowledge alone is not enough.
Working knowledge of how frontier labs buy from and work with vendors.
A track record turning research into shipped product and revenue at scale.
Credibility in front of frontier-lab researchers.
Comfort as a public technical voice.
Bay Area base, with a live network in the Valley AI and security community.
Fluent working across the Israel time zone.

Nice to Have:

Hands-on with RL post-training, GRPO, agentic environments or eval harness design.
Prior time inside a frontier lab, a research organisation, or a vendor selling into one.
Experience being the first senior person on the ground in a new geography.

Alice is a trust, safety, and security company built for the AI era. We safeguard the communicative technologies people use to create, collaborate, and interact- whether with each other or with machines.

In a world where AI has fundamentally changed the nature of risk, Alice provides end-to-end coverage across the entire AI lifecycle. We support frontier model labs, enterprises, and UGC platforms with a comprehensive suite of solutions: from model hardening evaluations and pre-deployment red-teaming to runtime guardrails and ongoing drift detection.

Alice is widely considered a global leader in online safety and AI security. We have some of the most forward-thinking and passionate minds in the world working to safeguard over 3 billion users across the largest AI and tech platforms.

If you're creative and driven to secure the future of AI, we want to hear from you!

jobs.title: Senior Solutions Architect, GovTech ISVs
jobs.description:
Description

Across state and local government, the software that powers everyday public services is being rebuilt around generative AI and agentic systems. AWS is hiring a Senior Solutions Architect (SA) to help Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) reimagine their products on AWS.

You will work directly with the leadership and engineering teams of ISVs whose software runs 911 dispatch, digital evidence, court case management, permitting and licensing, and benefits eligibility.

Your customer is a commercial software company. Their customer is a government agency. Their end user is a constituent.

This is an advisory role, focused on generative AI, agentic architectures, and the data foundations that make both work in regulated environments. You own the technical relationship with a portfolio of GovTech ISVs, and you lead the architectural deep dives that shape what they build. It is hands-on in a specific way. You will build prototypes and reference implementations, demonstrate that a pattern works before an ISV commits to it, and unblock their engineers when they are stuck. You will NOT ship production features in their product.

The work starts with discovery. You ask about the platform, the constraints, and the requirements the ISV's government buyers impose, and you challenge the assumptions before you design to it. Much of the work is foundational: compute selection, well-modeled data across relational, NoSQL, and analytics stores, networking, identity, and cost at scale. The AI capabilities your customers want to ship are only as good as the platforms underneath them, so you will spend time on those primitives. You are effective when your ISV ships a better product on AWS.

Ability to travel up to 30%.

Key job responsibilities

Guide ISV architecture decisions across compute, data, networking, identity, and databases. Advise on the trade-offs and prescribe a solution.
Run discovery with ISV engineering and product teams to understand their platform, their constraints, and their customers' requirements before recommending an architecture path.
Lead generative AI work on Amazon Bedrock: agentic patterns, retrieval-augmented generation, guardrails, evaluation, and responsible AI practices that hold up in a public sector procurement review.
Help ISVs turn AI prototypes into production systems that meet the bar their public sector buyers require.
Help ISVs modernize legacy platforms onto AWS with phased strategies such as strangler fig, replatforming, and domain decomposition.
Explain how compliance shapes architecture in regulated state and local environments, including CJIS, StateRAMP, FedRAMP, HIPAA, and data residency.
Communicate architecture decisions to ISV CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and government CIOs. Structure the trade-off discussion, defend the recommendation, and adjust depth to the audience.
Help ISVs adopt AI-assisted development tools such as Kiro and Amazon Q Developer to accelerate their own engineering teams.

About The Team

The GovTech Solutions Architecture team's mission is to be the best technology enabler for the ISVs who build software for state and local government and public safety. The work is technical, but the impact is human. The applications our customers ship affect how a citizen renews a license, how an investigator works a case, how a first responder gets dispatched. We take that seriously, and we look for teammates who do too.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

8+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
5+ years of cloud based solution (AWS or equivalent), system, network and operating system experience, or AWS Professional level certification
Experience facilitating discussions with senior leadership regarding technical / architectural trade-offs, best practices, and risk mitigation
Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
Experience working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage
Experience with designing and building applications using container and serverless technologies

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with enterprise software companies
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
Demonstrated use of AI-assisted development tools (Kiro, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar) to scale your own technical output.

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.

The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

jobs.description:
Position : Agentic AI Coach

Location : Minnesota

C2C

Role Overview

The Agentic AI Coach will play a hands on role in designing, coaching, and operationalizing agentic AI solutions for healthcare clients. This role bridges AI engineering, consulting delivery, and change enablement, ensuring AI agents are not only built correctly but are adopted, governed, and embedded into real business workflows.

You will work closely with AI architects, healthcare SMEs, and client stakeholders to guide the implementation, orchestration, and responsible use of AI agents across payer operations, analytics, testing, and automation use cases.

Key Responsibilities

Agentic AI Enablement & Coaching

Coach delivery teams and clients on how to design, deploy, and operate agentic AI systems, including task decomposition, autonomy levels, guardrails, and human in the loop patterns.

Guide teams on best practices for agent orchestration, memory, planning, tool usage, and escalation logic.

Support adoption of agentic AI operating models, including agent lifecycle management, monitoring, and continuous improvement.

Solution Delivery & Client Engagement

Partner with AI Architects and Consultants to translate business problems into agent based solutions, particularly across payer workflows (claims, prior auth, care management, analytics, testing, ops).

Participate in client workshops, solution walkthroughs, and demos, explaining agent behavior, outcomes, and limitations in business friendly language.

Support delivery of agent enabled assessments, pilots, and scaled implementations.

Responsible AI & Governance

Ensure agentic solutions align with Optum's AI governance, security, and compliance standards, including explainability, auditability, and risk controls.

Help teams define agent guardrails, approval thresholds, and failure handling to minimize operational and compliance risk.

Contribute to governance artifacts such as agent design reviews, risk assessments, and usage guidelines.

Platform & Tooling Support

Work with platforms such as Azure OpenAI, orchestration frameworks, and internal Optum agentic platforms to support delivery teams.

Assist in configuring agent monitoring, telemetry, and performance metrics.

Support integration of agents with enterprise systems (APIs, data platforms, workflow tools).

Required Qualifications

47 years of experience in AI, data, automation, or digital consulting roles.

Hands on exposure to GenAI / LLM based systems, including prompt design, tool calling, or workflow automation.

Practical understanding of agentic AI concepts: autonomy levels, planning, memory, orchestration, and human in the loop patterns.

Experience working in healthcare payer or provider environments (claims, UM/CM, analytics, ops preferred).

Strong communication skills with the ability to coach both technical teams and business stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting or delivering AI pilots, PoCs, or scaled implementations.

Familiarity with Responsible AI, governance, or compliance considerations in regulated industries.

Exposure to Azure, cloud platforms, or MLOps concepts.

Consulting experience within healthcare, insurance, or life sciences.

jobs.title: GenAI CBRNE Cyber Security Expert
jobs.description:
As a GenAI CBRNE & Cyber Red Team Expert, you'll adversarially test and strengthen the safety guardrails of GenAI systems against high-risk cyber threats - with a particular focus on industrial hacking, SCADA systems, ICS/OT environments, and CBRNE domains.

Drawing on deep industrial cybersecurity expertise (hands-on familiarity with SCADA, Modbus, DNP3, and PLC exploits) alongside CBRNE domain knowledge and advanced AI red-teaming skills, you'll design sophisticated adversarial prompts, multi-turn attack scenarios, jailbreaks, and model evaluations to determine when GenAI systems could materially enable physical-world industrial attacks or cyber-enabled CBRNE threats.

The role calls for an adversarial mindset: thinking like a malicious actor to find ways AI systems could be manipulated, combining seemingly benign information across interactions, circumventing safeguards, or exploiting model behavior to extract sensitive cyber-CBRNE information.

Key Responsibilities

Run rigorous red-teaming of GenAI models across SCADA, ICS, and CBRNE scenarios. You will be probing for safeguard bypasses, dangerous capability escalation, and unintended disclosure of sensitive OT information.
Design adversarial prompts, jailbreaks, and multi-turn evaluations against industrial hacking scenarios (SCADA, PLCs, DCS, Modbus/DNP3/IEC 60870-5-104/Ethernet-IP, critical infrastructure, hazardous-material facilities).
Evaluate whether models can be manipulated into assisting attacks via payload generation, ladder logic exploitation, reconnaissance, or aggregating benign inputs into high-risk workflows.
Document failure modes (obfuscation, role-play, decomposition, escalation), classify severity, and report findings to safety/alignment teams.
Build repeatable test suites, adversarial datasets, and risk taxonomies; stay current on GenAI attack techniques and CBRNE/critical-infrastructure threats.

Requirements

Must be US-based and authorized to work (excluding IL, TX)
Advanced degree in Cybersecurity, CS, Engineering, Security Studies, CBRNE sciences, or related field - or equivalent professional/military/government experience
Deep industrial cybersecurity expertise: SCADA, ICS/OT, industrial protocols (Modbus, DNP3, Ethernet/IP, Profinet), PLCs, cyber-physical attack chains
Strong CBRNE knowledge, especially its intersection with cyber/digital systems
Red-team experience: penetration testing, adversarial simulation, vulnerability research, or offensive security
GenAI red-teaming experience or aptitude: adversarial prompts, jailbreak research, multi-turn testing, LLM safety evaluation
Practical SCADA/OT hacking exposure: vulnerability research, protocol fuzzing, network architecture analysis
Adversarial mindset for identifying safeguard circumvention via decomposition, obfuscation, or multi-turn manipulation
Strong technical writing for documenting methodology, findings, and mitigations

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on LLM red-teaming, AI safety evals, or jailbreak/prompt research
Experience building red-team test cases, datasets, benchmarks, or evaluation pipelines
Familiarity with frontier AI safety concepts, dangerous-capability evals, and responsible scaling frameworks
Background in offensive security, threat intel, incident response, or adversary emulation
Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK (incl. ICS), NIST frameworks, IEC 62443
Experience in national security, defense, intelligence, or high-consequence industrial environments
Relevant offensive-security or ICS/OT certifications
Deep expertise in one or more: GenAI cyber red-teaming; SCADA/ICS/OT red-teaming; chemical/industrial cyber risk; biological/lab cyber risk; radiological/nuclear cyber risk; or cyber-physical/high-consequence threat analysis

The salary range for this role in the US is $150K - $178K - Range may vary based on experience. Salary at the time of offer will be commensurate with experience.

new_jobs.title: Senior Solutions Architect, GovTech ISVs
new_jobs.description:
Description

Across state and local government, the software that powers everyday public services is being rebuilt around generative AI and agentic systems. AWS is hiring a Senior Solutions Architect (SA) to help Independent Software Vendors (ISVs) reimagine their products on AWS.

You will work directly with the leadership and engineering teams of ISVs whose software runs 911 dispatch, digital evidence, court case management, permitting and licensing, and benefits eligibility.

Your customer is a commercial software company. Their customer is a government agency. Their end user is a constituent.

This is an advisory role, focused on generative AI, agentic architectures, and the data foundations that make both work in regulated environments. You own the technical relationship with a portfolio of GovTech ISVs, and you lead the architectural deep dives that shape what they build. It is hands-on in a specific way. You will build prototypes and reference implementations, demonstrate that a pattern works before an ISV commits to it, and unblock their engineers when they are stuck. You will NOT ship production features in their product.

The work starts with discovery. You ask about the platform, the constraints, and the requirements the ISV's government buyers impose, and you challenge the assumptions before you design to it. Much of the work is foundational: compute selection, well-modeled data across relational, NoSQL, and analytics stores, networking, identity, and cost at scale. The AI capabilities your customers want to ship are only as good as the platforms underneath them, so you will spend time on those primitives. You are effective when your ISV ships a better product on AWS.

Ability to travel up to 30%.

Key job responsibilities

Guide ISV architecture decisions across compute, data, networking, identity, and databases. Advise on the trade-offs and prescribe a solution.
Run discovery with ISV engineering and product teams to understand their platform, their constraints, and their customers' requirements before recommending an architecture path.
Lead generative AI work on Amazon Bedrock: agentic patterns, retrieval-augmented generation, guardrails, evaluation, and responsible AI practices that hold up in a public sector procurement review.
Help ISVs turn AI prototypes into production systems that meet the bar their public sector buyers require.
Help ISVs modernize legacy platforms onto AWS with phased strategies such as strangler fig, replatforming, and domain decomposition.
Explain how compliance shapes architecture in regulated state and local environments, including CJIS, StateRAMP, FedRAMP, HIPAA, and data residency.
Communicate architecture decisions to ISV CTOs, VPs of Engineering, and government CIOs. Structure the trade-off discussion, defend the recommendation, and adjust depth to the audience.
Help ISVs adopt AI-assisted development tools such as Kiro and Amazon Q Developer to accelerate their own engineering teams.

About The Team

The GovTech Solutions Architecture team's mission is to be the best technology enabler for the ISVs who build software for state and local government and public safety. The work is technical, but the impact is human. The applications our customers ship affect how a citizen renews a license, how an investigator works a case, how a first responder gets dispatched. We take that seriously, and we look for teammates who do too.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS?

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture

AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

Basic Qualifications

8+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience
5+ years of cloud based solution (AWS or equivalent), system, network and operating system experience, or AWS Professional level certification
Experience facilitating discussions with senior leadership regarding technical / architectural trade-offs, best practices, and risk mitigation
Experience contributing to engineering discussions around technology decisions and strategy related to a product
Experience working with Data & AI related technologies, including, but not limited to, AI/ML, GenAI, Analytics, Database, and/or Storage
Experience with designing and building applications using container and serverless technologies

Preferred Qualifications

Experience working with enterprise software companies
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
Demonstrated use of AI-assisted development tools (Kiro, Cursor, Claude Code, or similar) to scale your own technical output.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. new_jobs.title: GenAI CBRNE Cyber Security Expert
new_jobs.description:
As a GenAI CBRNE & Cyber Red Team Expert, you'll adversarially test and strengthen the safety guardrails of GenAI systems against high-risk cyber threats - with a particular focus on industrial hacking, SCADA systems, ICS/OT environments, and CBRNE domains.

Drawing on deep industrial cybersecurity expertise (hands-on familiarity with SCADA, Modbus, DNP3, and PLC exploits) alongside CBRNE domain knowledge and advanced AI red-teaming skills, you'll design sophisticated adversarial prompts, multi-turn attack scenarios, jailbreaks, and model evaluations to determine when GenAI systems could materially enable physical-world industrial attacks or cyber-enabled CBRNE threats.

The role calls for an adversarial mindset: thinking like a malicious actor to find ways AI systems could be manipulated, combining seemingly benign information across interactions, circumventing safeguards, or exploiting model behavior to extract sensitive cyber-CBRNE information.

Key Responsibilities

Run rigorous red-teaming of GenAI models across SCADA, ICS, and CBRNE scenarios. You will be probing for safeguard bypasses, dangerous capability escalation, and unintended disclosure of sensitive OT information.
Design adversarial prompts, jailbreaks, and multi-turn evaluations against industrial hacking scenarios (SCADA, PLCs, DCS, Modbus/DNP3/IEC 60870-5-104/Ethernet-IP, critical infrastructure, hazardous-material facilities).
Evaluate whether models can be manipulated into assisting attacks via payload generation, ladder logic exploitation, reconnaissance, or aggregating benign inputs into high-risk workflows.
Document failure modes (obfuscation, role-play, decomposition, escalation), classify severity, and report findings to safety/alignment teams.
Build repeatable test suites, adversarial datasets, and risk taxonomies; stay current on GenAI attack techniques and CBRNE/critical-infrastructure threats.

Requirements

Must be US-based and authorized to work (excluding IL, TX)
Advanced degree in Cybersecurity, CS, Engineering, Security Studies, CBRNE sciences, or related field - or equivalent professional/military/government experience
Deep industrial cybersecurity expertise: SCADA, ICS/OT, industrial protocols (Modbus, DNP3, Ethernet/IP, Profinet), PLCs, cyber-physical attack chains
Strong CBRNE knowledge, especially its intersection with cyber/digital systems
Red-team experience: penetration testing, adversarial simulation, vulnerability research, or offensive security
GenAI red-teaming experience or aptitude: adversarial prompts, jailbreak research, multi-turn testing, LLM safety evaluation
Practical SCADA/OT hacking exposure: vulnerability research, protocol fuzzing, network architecture analysis
Adversarial mindset for identifying safeguard circumvention via decomposition, obfuscation, or multi-turn manipulation
Strong technical writing for documenting methodology, findings, and mitigations

Preferred Qualifications

Hands-on LLM red-teaming, AI safety evals, or jailbreak/prompt research
Experience building red-team test cases, datasets, benchmarks, or evaluation pipelines
Familiarity with frontier AI safety concepts, dangerous-capability evals, and responsible scaling frameworks
Background in offensive security, threat intel, incident response, or adversary emulation
Familiarity with MITRE ATT&CK (incl. ICS), NIST frameworks, IEC 62443
Experience in national security, defense, intelligence, or high-consequence industrial environments
Relevant offensive-security or ICS/OT certifications
Deep expertise in one or more: GenAI cyber red-teaming; SCADA/ICS/OT red-teaming; chemical/industrial cyber risk; biological/lab cyber risk; radiological/nuclear cyber risk; or cyber-physical/high-consequence threat analysis
